Subject: Finova discovery — SLOs & regional routing recap

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goals you shared: 99th percentile generation latency <= 250ms for US web traffic; 95th percentile <= 350ms in EU; APAC target is a bit looser (P95 < 600ms) as you’re piloting there.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~120 QPS (text-generation non-streaming) with peak bursts to ~300 QPS during business hours.
- Concurrency: typical per-instance concurrency ~50 concurrent sessions; some endpoints will need up to 200 concurrent short-lived streams.
- Streaming: product team wants server-side streaming for chat UX (token-by-token) with sub-200ms first-byte latency target for streaming start.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU for processing and logs, APAC pilot requires data residency in Singapore for a subset of traffic.

Action items: 
1) Can Rishi/Aditya confirm feasibility of the latency/throughput numbers and give a short plan for regional routing (multi-region active-active vs geo-proxy)?
2) We’ll prepare a short SLO summary doc and a proposed mutual action plan.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive next week to validate streaming perf and KV cache behavior.

Ethan — are those targets accurate from your side? Any additional constraints (certs, audit windows) we should note?

Best,

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Finova discovery — SLOs & regional routing recap

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa — adding technical detail from the serving/runtime side. TL;DR: targets are achievable with a hybrid active-active routing design and careful placement of model variants + caching.

Notes by topic:

Latency & throughput
- US (primary): 99p <= 250ms is achievable using our low-latency model variant (quantized FP16 kernels) with autoscaling to meet sustained 120 QPS and burst to 300 QPS. We recommend reserved Dedicated capacity for predictable tail latency.
- EU: aim for P95 <= 350ms; deploy EU model replicas + KV prefix cache close to EU region. If you need strict EU-only processing for certain endpoints, we can pin routes to EU-only model pools.
- APAC: P95 < 600ms is reasonable for Singapore region; for Tokyo we see slightly higher tail latencies depending on model size.

Concurrency & streaming
- Streaming start (first-byte): sub-200ms is possible if the request hits a warm KV cache or warm model instance. Cold-starts can add 200-400ms depending on instance state. We’ll propose a warm-pool configuration and pre-warming policies for your chat endpoints.
- For high-concurrency short streams (up to 200 concurrent), we recommend continuous batching disabled for those routes and set dedicated concurrency slots to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Regional routing & data residency
- Multi-region routing patterns we support:
  1) Active-active with per-request geo routing (lowest latency, requires synchronized model versions and global KV replication for stateful prefixes).
  2) Geo-proxy (edge routing to nearest region, fall back to central region if capacity insufficient).
  3) Per-tenant routing (strict residency): pin tenant to region for all processing and logs.
- For your EU residency requirement, we’d use per-tenant routing + EU-only logging (no cross-region log replication). For APAC pilot: route subset of requests to SG cluster; keep analytics aggregated in US if that’s acceptable.

Monitoring & SLOs
- We’ll export per-region token latency histograms, per-route throughput, and tail latency traces. Can set automated alerts if P95/P99 crosses thresholds and auto-scale rules trigger.

Open questions
- Do you need synchronous sync of KV prefixes across regions or is eventual consistency acceptable for your UX?
- Any regulatory requirements around log retention periods (e.g., 30/90/365 days)?

I can put together an internal proposal (1–2 pages) with recommended deployment pattern and cost/latency trade-offs — aiming to share by EOD tomorrow.

—Aditya

Thanks Marissa / Aditya — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: EU tenant data must remain within EU for both inference and logs. We cannot replicate logs to US. For APAC pilot, Singapore residency is required for the subset flagged as APAC (we can tag those requests).
- KV consistency: eventual consistency is okay for non-sensitive session state; for auth decisions we need strong consistency.
- Retention: security wants 365-day audit logs for production. Will this be supported in EU-only retention?
- Certificate / compliance: can you confirm SOC2 in-scope and if you have a recent ISO statement? We’ll raise as part of procurement.

We’re happy to see the internal proposal. If you can also include a rough cost delta between active-active vs geo-proxy for the first year, that would help our finance team.
